log_parsing.label: Log Parsing
log_parsing.blurb: Turn raw log lines into templates, masking every variable part.
log_parsing.measures: Given production log lines, replace IDs, timestamps, paths and durations with <*> while keeping constant words exactly. This is the foundation of every log pipeline. It is how you group millions of lines into a handful of event types.
log_parsing.scoring: 0.5 x exact-template accuracy + 0.5 x token-level F1 against ground truth.
log_parsing.source: Real Loghub 2k logs (HDFS, BGL, OpenSSH, Apache, Zookeeper, Linux) with the official ground-truth templates from logpai/logparser.
log_parsing.hard: Some templates are entirely constant. Models that over-wildcard everything lose points, so it rewards restraint as much as detection.

anomaly_detection.label: Anomaly Detection
anomaly_detection.blurb: Flag which log lines are genuinely anomalous, and which only look scary.
anomaly_detection.measures: Given a window of logs, identify the anomalous lines by index. Routine warnings, retries and rolling-restart noise must be left alone.
anomaly_detection.scoring: Precision / recall / F1 over per-line labels.
anomaly_detection.source: Real labelled BGL supercomputer windows plus hard synthetic cases.
anomaly_detection.hard: BGL labels 'instruction cache parity error corrected' as NORMAL, so grepping for 'error' scores about 40. One case is a healthy service where the correct answer is zero anomalies: over-flagging scores 0. Another is silent data loss with no error keyword anywhere.

pattern_correlation.label: Pattern & Correlation
pattern_correlation.blurb: Group related events and work out which failure caused which.
pattern_correlation.measures: Identify recurring problem patterns across services, then the causal links between them: the A causes B causes C cascade behind a multi-service incident.
pattern_correlation.scoring: 0.6 x pattern coverage + 0.4 x correlation accuracy.
pattern_correlation.source: Curated multi-service cascades with distractors and 2-hop causal chains.
pattern_correlation.hard: Unrelated failures happen inside the same window and must not be wired into the causal chain.

metrics_timeseries.label: Metrics Time-Series
metrics_timeseries.blurb: Spot anomalies in a seasonal metric series.
metrics_timeseries.measures: Given 96 points of a metric on a daily cycle, find the indices that deviate from expected seasonal behaviour (spikes, dips and level shifts).
metrics_timeseries.scoring: Point-wise precision / recall / F1 with a +/-1 index tolerance.
metrics_timeseries.source: Seasonal series with injected anomalies, including two clean series.
metrics_timeseries.hard: The series follow a daily cycle, so a global z-score misses off-peak spikes and level shifts. Some anomalies are smaller than the seasonal swing itself.

root_cause.label: Root Cause & Summary
root_cause.blurb: Explain the incident: what happened, the impact, and why.
root_cause.measures: From an incident's logs, name the root cause in one sentence and write a short postmortem summary.
root_cause.scoring: 0.4 ROUGE-L on the summary + 0.3 ROUGE-1 on the root cause + 0.3 keyword recall. An optional LLM-as-judge can replace the blend.
root_cause.hard: Each incident contains red herrings (unrelated deploys, failing crons, network blips) that happened in the window and must be ruled out.

multimodal_rca.label: Multi-modal RCA
multimodal_rca.blurb: Localize the culprit service across metrics, logs and traces at once.
multimodal_rca.measures: Given per-service metrics, logs and trace aggregates from a real microservice incident, name the culprit service from a closed candidate list, classify the fault, and cite the evidence that supports it. Three verdicts are possible and choosing between them is most of the task: a service, "none" (the system is healthy), or "unknown" (something is wrong but this evidence does not show what).
multimodal_rca.scoring: 0.40 culprit localization + 0.25 fault type + 0.25 modality grounding + 0.10 evidence recall.
multimodal_rca.source: Real incidents from the Nezha dataset (FSE 2023) on OnlineBoutique and TrainTicket, plus five faults whose culprit is unrecoverable from the evidence and one healthy baseline.
multimodal_rca.hard: The informative modality changes case to case. CPU faults show up in the metrics and leave the logs ordinary; code-level faults surface only in the logs. Citing a modality that shows nothing costs precision, so 'cite everything' cannot win. A metrics-only heuristic scores 100 on the CPU cases and 0 on the log-only ones. Five cases go further: a fault really was injected, but it is buried in every channel, and the calibrated answer is 'unknown'. Naming a plausible-looking service there scores 10 out of 100. The rule-based baseline does exactly that on all five.

efficiency.label: Efficiency & Consistency
efficiency.blurb: Speed, token thrift and run-to-run stability.
efficiency.measures: Derived from the runs above rather than its own dataset.
efficiency.scoring: 0.4 speed (against a 20s budget) + 0.3 token thrift (against 4000 tokens) + 0.3 run-to-run score stability.
efficiency.source: Computed from every other category's runs.
efficiency.hard: A model that is accurate but slow and verbose pays for it here.

datasets.source: Nezha microservice incidents (metrics + logs + traces): 12 solvable, 5 where the culprit is unrecoverable, 1 healthy baseline
